newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO campaigns for global sanctions against Israel.
newsitem.headline: PLO campaigns for global sanctions against Israel.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority on Saturday called for an emergency meeting of the United Nations General Assembly to impose sanctions against Israel to force it to respect international law.

"As a result of the freezing of the peace process by Israel, its settlement aggression on Palestinian land and against our people, the Palestinian Authority calls for an immediate emergency meeting of the United Nations General Assembly to impose economic and political sanctions against Israel to compel it to respect international law," said a statement issued early on Saturday after a weekly cabinet meeting.
Israeli-Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) peace moves have been frozen since Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat dispatched top PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat to New York with letters for world leaders slated to attend a U.N. environment summit next week.
"I will stress the need to revive peace efforts and to put an end to Israeli settlement policies," Erekat told Reuters.
Three months of deadlock last week erupted into daily clashes between stone-throwing Palestinians and Israeli troops in the West Bank city of Hebron. Some 150 Arabs have been wounded in the unrest.
The Authority warned that patience among the Palestinian public over Jewish settlement on lands Israel occupied in 1967 was growing thin.

"The Palestinian Authority condemned Israeli troops for firing live and rubber bullets and teargas at our people...who are defending their land threatened by the crawling settlements," the statement said.

The violence erupted in Hebron last Saturday after a U.S. congressional vote demanded President Bill Clinton recognise Arab East Jerusalem -- occupied by Israel in 1967 and revered by Palestinians as the capital of their future state -- as part of the capital of the Jewish state.
Israel claims all Jerusalem as its capital and says it has the right to settle the West Bank and Gaza. Its claims have failed to win international recognition.

"The Palestinian Authority condemns and denounces the decision of the American Congress over Jerusalem which is a dangerous and serious violation of international legitimacy and harms United States credibility as co-sponsor of the peace process," the cabinet statement said.
